The news is quite intriguing. ChatGPT's latest update adds new Mac integration features, capable of handling conversations from Apple's "Messages" app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now includes the Apple "Messages" plugin

The new Apple "Messages" plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, as well as compose and send messages. OpenAI stated that the feature is available across all plans of the macOS ChatGPT desktop application, and supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This level of access raises questions about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that sending actions require user confirmation by default. Users should carefully consider before granting persistent authorisation. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the associated risks, how to revoke access, and a known issue involving tasks that disable confirmation prompts.

Currently, this feature is only available on Macs equipped with Apple Silicon; Intel models are not yet supported.

Website co-editing, shared conversation snapshots, and other features

Although the "Messages" plugin is the most anticipated new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations can now sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, allowing users to access important conversations on both Mac and iPhone whenever needed.

ChatGPT has also added a feature allowing users to share read-only local Codex conversation snapshots. These snapshots do not change as the original conversation updates.

Links created with personal accounts can be accessed by anyone who has the URL, while workspace links are restricted to members of that workspace. OpenAI states that Codex will redact known sensitive formats, but reminds users to review snapshots themselves, as they may still contain sensitive information.

Additionally, website owners can invite active members of the same workspace to co-edit websites that support collaboration. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner completes the initial publication. Owners retain control over access permissions, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some website owners can also change URLs hosted by ChatGPT without redeployment, and old URLs will automatically redirect to the new URLs.

Finally, the "Computer History" feature launched last week is expanding to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This optional feature requires "Memories" to be enabled and is off by default.

You can read the full release notes for this update here.
